results.title: If you picked your H100 provider on price, the answer changed, and nobody lowered a rate to make it change. | Bobby Clay
results.author: Bobby Clay
highlights:
# If you picked your H100 provider on price, the answer changed, and nobody lowered a rate to make it change. | Bobby Clay · LinkedIn · 2026-10-21T00:00:00+00:00

**Bobby Clay**.

---

If you picked your H100 provider on price, the answer changed, and nobody lowered a rate to make it change.

Crusoe’s published H100 read $3.90 in our October 11 catalog and $4.50 in our October 18 catalog. Lambda’s read $3.99 in both. So the lowest published H100 across the nine providers we track rose to $3.99, and the company that now sets it never touched its price.

Crusoe was the only one of those nine whose published price differed between the two catalogs. Its H200 moved the same way, $4.29 to $5.40 across the same two.

Underneath that, the Ornn Compute Price Index, a third-party index of traded prices rather than quoted or listed ones, rose in all four families between its October 11 and October 19 readings. B200 is the clearest case. No provider published anything, and the distance between the lowest published B200 across those nine and the index still more than doubled, from $0.76 on October 11 to $1.72 against the October 19 reading.

One pricing page changed. The market moved on all four.

Nine providers, every figure dated.

# If you’re budgeting for AI infrastructure, I’d take another look at the GPU pricing assumptions before signing the next contract. | John Barger · LinkedIn · 2026-10-28T00:00:00+00:00

**John Barger**.

---

If you’re budgeting for AI infrastructure, I’d take another look at the GPU pricing assumptions before signing the next contract.

Bobby Clay’s October 26 update gives a good reason to check. Crusoe’s published H200 rate fell from $5.40 to $4.29 per GPU-hour. Meanwhile, B200’s transaction-based price index rose 16.1% in a week to $9.76 per GPU-hour, while the lowest published B200 rate across the nine providers he tracks stayed at $6.69.

That gap would have me asking a few questions. Is the listed rate available in the region and configuration I need? Can I actually get the capacity?

## List prices are a starting point.

Send us your requirement and we'll return up to 3 actual quotes from EU-resident providers within 48 hours. Free for buyers.

results.title: Nebius did exactly what it said it would. Last week's Pulse flagged the on-demand increases Nebius had posted for October 1. Our October 4 catalog capture yesterday shows them in place, in … | Bobby Clay
results.author: Bobby Clay
highlights:
# Nebius did exactly what it said it would. Last week's Pulse flagged the on-demand increases Nebius had posted for October 1. Our October 4 catalog capture yesterday shows them in place, in … | Bobby Clay · LinkedIn · 2026-10-05T00:00:00+00:00

**Bobby Clay**.

---

Nebius did exactly what it said it would. Last week's Pulse flagged the on-demand increases Nebius had posted for October 1. Our October 4 catalog capture yesterday shows them in place, in dollars per GPU-hour:

H100: $3.85 to $4.50
H200: $4.50 to $5.40
B200: $7.15 to $8.50
B300: $7.85 to $9.50

That changed the lowest observed H100 list price across the nine providers we track. On September 27 it was Nebius at $3.85 per GPU-hour. On October 4 it was Crusoe at $3.90.
Everything else held. Of 14,001 GPU price listings in the October 4 catalog, 13,996 matched a September 27 listing, and the 20 Nebius listings were the only verified changes above 1%.

The transaction side moved on its own path. OCPI for H200 went from $4.84 on September 28 to $5.57 on October 4. Over the same stretch, the lowest H200 list price we track held at $4.29 (Crusoe). List prices and transaction prices measure different things, and this week the gap between them widened. If you buy on-demand capacity from a Neocloud, posted price notices are worth tracking. This one landed on schedule, to the cent.

The full issue, with every provider's lowest observed price and the method notes, is here:
https://lnkd.in/efqfwQWm

These are public catalog list prices, not live quotes, and a listing does not establish capacity or orderability.

results.title: The H100 got more expensive · Three Phase. Potentia Intelligence.
results.author: Jose Mir
highlights:
### One Big Thing · Phase 3 · Compute

What happened: Nebius raised on-demand GPU prices on October 1, its second hike in about three months. Independent trackers show the same direction across the market.

Why it matters: The bear case on AI infrastructure assumed GPUs lose value fast. Rental rates are the cleanest test of that assumption, and so far the test is failing.

By the numbers:

- Nebius list price for an H100 went from $3.85 to $4.50 per GPU-hour; B300 from $7.85 to $9.50.
- The Ornn H100 index settled at $3.17 on October 23, up about 4% in a month.

results.title: Neocloud vs hyperscaler GPU: what capacity costs | Casitel
highlights:
Neocloud vs hyperscaler GPU rates for the H100, H200 and B200, read on 3 November 2026, with published commitment discounts and what else changes the bill.

C Compute · H100 list rates, per GPU-hour Rates read 3 November 2026

$3.99 lowest H100 rate in this note, at Lambda and E2E Networks

Each provider's own page, read 3 November 2026. Not executed prices.

...

A neocloud is a cloud built around GPUs. Newcomer, writing in May 2026, names Lambda and Crusoe as neoclouds that own their chips and sell the compute. CoreWeave and Nebius are two more. Regional ones sit in other markets: E2E Networks in India and Sakura Internet in Japan both publish GPU rates and commitment terms.

...

## What the rate cards say

All rates below are US dollars per GPU-hour, taken from each provider's own page on 3 November 2026. They are list rates. They are not what large buyers sign.

Provider H100 H200 B200 What the rate is

Lambda$3.99 Not listed$6.69 On-demand, 8-GPU instance

E2E Networks$3.99$5.29$7.99 On-demand

Nebius$4.50$5.40$8.50 On-demand, HGX

CoreWeave$6.16$6.31$8.60 On-demand, North America

AWS$5.97$6.87$14.21 Capacity Blocks, a short reservation

Google Cloud$9.80$10.71 Not read Vertex AI, managed service

Oracle$10.00$10.00$14.00 Pay as you go

Microsoft Azure$12.29 Not read Not read ND H100 v5, East US

Three of these need a note. CoreWeave and Azure price a whole 8-GPU machine by the hour: $49.24 and $98.32 for the H100. The per-GPU figures above are our own arithmetic. AWS publishes a plain on-demand rate only in its calculator, so the AWS row is its Capacity Blocks price, and for the H200 it is the p5e machine (the p5en costs $7.90). Google's row is the Vertex AI managed service, which is not the same product as a bare virtual machine.

Even so, the spread is wide. The H100 runs from $3.99 to $12.29, about three times. The B200 runs from $6.69 to $14.21, about twice. Rate cards also move. In our read on 8 October, Nebius showed $3.85 for an H100. On 3 November it showed $4.50.

## What commitments change

Every provider here says a commitment lowers the rate. Few publish by how much.

C Compute · published commitment discounts Read 3 Nov 2026

E2E Networks 10% to 30%, its own figure

Sakura Internet 5% for 6 months, 10% for 12

Each provider's own pages, read 3 Nov 2026. Discounts off list rates.

- CoreWeave says it offers up to 60% off its on-demand prices for committed use. That is its own claim. The page lists no committed rate.
- Azure publishes reservation prices through its public price API. For the H100 machine in East US, the one-year price works out 36% below pay as you go and the three-year price 56% below. We divided each term price by its hours.
- Google Cloud lists Flexible Savings Plan rates on the Vertex AI page. For the H200 they are $9.64 for one year and $8.57 for three, which is 10% and 20% below $10.71.
- E2E Networks says three-month, six-month and annual commitments can earn 10% to 30%, depending on length and volume.
- Sakura Internet announced on 1 July 2026 a commitment plan for one H100 plan: 5% off for six months and 10% off for twelve.
- AWS cut P5 (H100) prices by 44% for on-demand and 45% for the three-year Instance Savings Plan from 1 June 2025. Those are cuts from its earlier prices, not discounts off today's rate.
- Nebius and Lambda name no percentage. Both point large buyers to sales.
